headline: EMT Sprints 1.5 Miles Uphill With Blood to Save Dying Climber
meta_description: When a rock climber fell 20 feet on North Carolina's Shortoff Mountain, an EMT volunteer ran 1,000 feet of elevation in 31 minutes carrying life-saving blood.
summary_short: Will Soper, a 28-year-old EMT, hiked 1.5 miles up 1,000 feet of elevation in 31 minutes carrying blood for a critically injured climber on Shortoff Mountain.
body:
When Jacob Gregory fell 20 feet down a rock face on North Carolina's Shortoff Mountain, he was bleeding internally and running out of time. Will Soper, a 28-year-old experienced climber and EMT volunteer for Burke Rescue Inc., was teaching a training course two hours away when he heard the dispatch. He immediately drove to the trailhead, understanding that this remote, notoriously challenging rescue would demand every available responder. By the time Soper arrived, first responders had already located Gregory in critical condition—but the situation was about to become far more urgent. Over his radio, Soper learned that Gregory needed blood transfusion immediately to replace what he was rapidly losing.

Without hesitation, Soper headed back down the mountain, packed blood bags into a cooler with ice and transfusion equipment, and turned back toward the slopes. The climb that followed was extraordinary: in just 30 minutes, Soper gained 1,000 feet of elevation over 1.5 miles, maintaining a fast hiking and jogging pace without stopping for breaks. His rock and ice climbing experience and physical conditioning proved crucial—he reached the rappel point where rescuers had positioned themselves, ready to lower him down to Gregory's location.

Gregory was transported to Atrium Carolinas Medical Center in Charlotte, where his recovery status remains uncertain. Yet his family's gratitude was unambiguous. "To every responder who answered that call: thank you," they wrote. "You saved a life and brought a husband, father, brother, son, friend, and loved one to safety." More than 20 agencies coordinated the rescue, but it was Soper's combination of skill, speed, and willingness to drop everything that made the difference between a recovery story and a tragedy. Soper now encourages others to train with their local rescue squads.
quick_facts: EMT ran 1.5 miles uphill, gaining 1,000 feet elevation in 31 minutes
Climber Jacob Gregory fell 20 feet on Shortoff Mountain, North Carolina
Will Soper, 28, carried blood transfusion supplies in a backpack
Over 20 agencies responded to the remote rescue operation
